title: 3 Solar Myths
purpose: Pinned Facebook post and paid brand-awareness/reach ads
premise: Three common solar myths, each busted with a checked fact, plus a follow call to action.
scriptBasis: Claude draft, owner picked concept C (3 Solar Myths) 2026-11-24 14:07 Manila; claims checked online 2026-11-24.

sources: Sources: U.S. DOE; NOAA; Meralco net metering & DER; ERC/DOE
interconnection standards; Fronius & SMA backup docs (checked 24 Nov 2026)

cues.text: Naniniwala ka pa ba sa tatlong solar myth na 'to?
Unang myth, hindi raw gumagana ang solar kapag maulap.
Ang totoo, bumababa lang ang output, pero may kuryente pa rin.
Pangalawang myth, kailangan daw laging may battery.
Ang totoo, gumagana ang grid-tied kahit walang battery.
Pangatlong myth, may kuryente ka raw kahit brownout.
Ang totoo, kusang namamatay ang grid-tied kapag brownout.
Para may ilaw, kailangan ng battery at backup wiring.
I-follow si Kuya SoLight para laging tama ang solar info mo!
Dahil ang gusto ni Kuya SoLight… naka-solar ka na, SoSmart ka pa!

sources.title: Solar-plus-storage / Homeowner's Guide to Going Solar
excerpts: Batteries can store solar energy produced during the day for use at night or during outages, if the system is designed for it.

sources.title: Net-Metering Rules and Interconnection Standards (Philippine Distribution Code framework)

sources.title: Backup power function
excerpts: Backup operation requires a compatible battery and the appropriate backup wiring/switching to separate the home circuits from the grid.

sources.title: Distributed Energy Resources
excerpts: At times when there is no sunlight, or at night, the grid will provide electricity.

sources.title: Solar and Net Metering
excerpts: Your system supplies the property first while it is generating.
The Meralco grid supplies the property when renewable generation is not enough.

sources.title: Solar energy and clouds

sources.title: Guerilla solar installations need to be controlled, says Philippine power distributor

sources.title: Battery-backup function
